about: Text limits for paid ads, per platform and field. 'max' is a hard cap the platform refuses past. 'recommended' is the length the platform says avoids truncation; longer text is allowed but may be cut off.

rules.wide: Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count 2.
rules.wide+emoji: Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters and emoji count 2.

platforms.name: Google Ads responsive display ad
platforms.notes: Up to 5 headlines, 5 descriptions, one long headline and one business name.

platforms.name: Microsoft Advertising responsive search ad
platforms.notes: 3 to 15 headlines and 2 to 4 descriptions. Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters and emoji count double, so a headline fits 15 of them.

platforms.name: Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads
platforms.notes: Meta publishes recommended lengths, not caps. Longer text is allowed but may be cut off, and some placements cut shorter still.

platforms.name: LinkedIn Sponsored Content (single image)
platforms.notes: Every field has a hard maximum and a shorter recommended length so the text is not truncated.

platforms.name: TikTok In-Feed ad
platforms.notes: Up to 4 lines of ad text show before 'See more'. TikTok suggests staying within 100 characters (50 in Chinese, Japanese or Korean, which count 2).

platforms.name: Pinterest ad
platforms.notes: The feed may show only the first 40 characters of a title (30 in double-byte scripts). Descriptions do not show in the home or search feed.

platforms.name: Reddit image ad
platforms.notes: Reddit recommends 100 characters or fewer for the headline, 80 or fewer to be safer from truncation.

platforms.name: X ad
platforms.notes: Each link in the post text costs 23 characters, whatever its length. A card headline over about 50 characters may wrap to two lines with an ellipsis.
